INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEW B of PR #30 at head 1a171c9a. Dispatched by cron, not by the author; I read only what is on GitHub and could not see the author's reasoning. Verdict DISAGREE on one blocking finding.

== BLOCKING 1: the merge commit silently reverted this PR's own HANDOFF.md work, and proof/30.json asserts that work as a mutation it did not make ==

Three commits on this branch rewrite HANDOFF.md's "In flight" section: a9def7f, a91843e (the audit correction that removes the pinned stale SHAs) and 2613df2 (regeneration). The merge commit 1a171c9 resolved HANDOFF.md entirely to main's side and discarded all three.

Reproduction:
  git diff --stat 5e7b08a HEAD -- HANDOFF.md docs/ proof/30.json
    -> HANDOFF.md | 63 +++--- (32 insertions, 31 deletions); NOTHING else changed
  diff <(git show origin/main:HANDOFF.md | sed '/lwb-handoff:begin/,/lwb-handoff:end/d') \
       <(sed '/lwb-handoff:begin/,/lwb-handoff:end/d' HANDOFF.md)
    -> IDENTICAL. Outside the generated block, HEAD's HANDOFF.md is byte-for-byte main's.

I verified the other four branch files were NOT touched by the merge (build-plan.md, decisions.md, session-handoff-2026-09-19.md, proof/30.json all unchanged 5e7b08a..HEAD). The loss is isolated to HANDOFF.md.

Why this is blocking rather than cosmetic:

(a) proof/30.json's `mutations` contains "HANDOFF.md: in-flight section rewritten for the post-#27 state and the live cloud loop; generated block regenerated". At HEAD the first half of that is false -- the in-flight section is not rewritten, it is main's. A proof record asserting a change that is not in the diff is the exact falsification this apparatus exists to prevent, and it is worse here than a stale sentence because the record is the artifact the gate treats as evidence.

(b) The PR's own thesis is that the plan the routines read is not on main. build-plan.md and D27 do land, so the conductor routine IS unblocked -- I want to be clear that the PR's core purpose succeeds. But HANDOFF.md is the file CLAUDE.md orders every session to read first, and at HEAD it still does not mention docs/requirements/build-plan.md at all. The branch commit that added the "THE PLAN IS docs/requirements/build-plan.md" pointer is the one the merge threw away.

(c) HEAD ships HANDOFF.md asserting "3. IN FLIGHT: #23 re-execute hardening, #24 open-PR post-merge" and "2. DONE. Proof of completion in CI: #17-#22". Both are stale -- #23 and #24 have proof records and merged, main is at #34 (#27, #31 landed). This staleness is inherited from main, not introduced here; the defect is that this PR claims to correct it and at HEAD does not.

Fix: re-apply the branch's HANDOFF.md in-flight rewrite on top of the merge, then regenerate the block LAST (see finding 2).

== BLOCKING-ADJACENT 2: the recorded main SHA survives on a one-commit tolerance and main has already moved ==

HANDOFF.md:44 records `main SHA: de27f723...`. lwb-check-state-claims passes today only because de27f723 happens to be live main's FIRST PARENT (live main is bfe85079). I confirmed the tolerance is exactly those two values by mutation probe: replacing the SHA with 0000... produced

  FAIL: HANDOFF.md:44: [stale main SHA in generated block] main SHA: 0000... (live: bfe85079..., live main's first parent: 'de27f723...')

so the check is NOT vacuous for SHA claims -- it genuinely fails on a wrong one. But one more commit landing on main moves the first parent to bfe85079 and turns this green INFO into a red FAIL with no further change to this branch. The PR is already mergeable_state=behind. Merge current main and regenerate the block as the LAST write.

== NON-BLOCKING 3: both the PR body and proof/30.json under-enumerate what decisions.md actually adds ==

proof/30.json `mutations` says "docs/requirements/decisions.md: D21, D22, D23, D24, D27". The PR body's bullet list names the same five. Measured:

  git diff origin/main..HEAD -- docs/requirements/decisions.md | grep '^+## '
    -> D21, D22, D23, D24, D25, D26, D27

D25 (efficiency claims are order-of-magnitude only) and D26 (first subjects for driving a real repo -- names external projects, records an owner exclusion of Watchtower) land unlisted in both places. A reviewer working from either enumeration would not know to read them. At file level the mutations list is complete, and proof/schema.json only asks for paths, so this does not fail any gate -- it is an accuracy defect in a volunteered content-level claim.

== NON-BLOCKING 4: D25's measured justification overstates what I can measure ==

D25 item 1 states: "The `tokens` block in every proof record is CUMULATIVE across PRs 12-27. One figure for sixteen deliverables. The record's own `source` field says so."

Measured across all 16 token-bearing records at HEAD:
  - There are 14 DISTINCT figures, not one. They are running cumulative totals of one session's whole spend, growing monotonically 13:265.8M -> 26:999.1M (with one non-monotonic step, 23:884.1M -> 24:875.5M).
  - proof/27.json and proof/30.json record "unknown", not a cumulative figure.
  - proof/31.json is a DIFFERENT session's own measured figure (9.2M input, 77 usage records, 598s) -- not cumulative across 12-27 at all.
  - There is no proof/12.json on this branch (records run 7-11, 13, 15-27, 30, 31), so "across PRs 12-27" names a record that does not exist.

D25's substantive point is correct and I am not disputing it: a cumulative per-session total cannot attribute cost to a deliverable, and the schema's own tokens.source description does say retries/setup_overhead/tool_overhead have no source on any current runtime (I verified that text at proof/schema.json:110). The decision D25 reaches is conservative, so the overstatement pushes toward caution rather than false confidence. But "one figure for sixteen deliverables" and "every proof record" are not what is on disk, in a document whose own framing is "measured not assumed", in a repo whose stated signature defect is a scoped claim stated as though repo-wide.

== NEAR-MISS I ALMOST FILED, RECORDED BECAUSE HIDING IT WOULD BE WORSE ==

I opened this review expecting the known ordering trap: the HANDOFF generator ran at 2613df2 and proof/30.json was added AFTER it at 5e7b08a, which should have left the count stale one commit later. I had the accusation drafted. It is WRONG. At 2613df2 the block said 18/18 with 20 records reachable, and the merge then replaced HANDOFF.md with main's copy, which says 21/21 -- and 21 is exactly the count at HEAD. The generator being out of order was neutralised by the very merge that caused finding 1. I verified the count by recomputation before writing anything. Had I filed it, I would have charged a correct number as stale.
